origin: hand-written from the published OpenAPI schema; every value invented
notes: A management key cannot call the completion endpoints, so its usage counters stay at zero and it carries no credit cap. is_management_key is the cheapest honest way to learn the presented key's permission category WITHOUT probing the balance - architecture forbids using inference calls to test authentication - the field is a published, required schema property, so its presence is documented; it is still unmeasured against a live response, and no code may depend on it until reconciliation confirms it. expires_at matters operationally: expiry is fixed at creation and cannot be extended, and an expired key makes every request fail 401 'API key expired', so rotation has to be scheduled ahead of it. A management key is account-scoped and unscoped across workspaces, and the same credential also unlocks destructive key, BYOK and guardrail routes - which is why the read-only allow-list has to be enforced in code. SCHEMA RE-VERIFICATION 2026-10-30: the authoritative OpenAPI schema for this route was read at https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/api-reference/api-keys/get-current-api-key. Its `data` object publishes 24 required fields; this fixture carries all of them plus the optional nullable `expires_at`. Three corrections follow. (1) `rate_limit` is not an invented sub-shape: the schema publishes it as an object with three typed, required properties (`interval` string, `requests` integer, `note` string) and marks the object `deprecated: true` with the description "Legacy rate limit information about a key. Will always return -1." That description contradicts the schema's own example values (1h / 1000), which are what this fixture reproduces, so the field must be parsed and discarded and never read as a live rate limit. (2) `organization_id` and `workspace_id` are required and are the documented account and workspace identity: `organization_id` is "null when an individual account owns it" and `workspace_id` is "null when no active workspace resolved for it, for example because the key's workspace was deleted". (3) `is_management_key`, `is_provisioning_key`, `expires_at`, `creator_user_id` and `allowed_data_regions` ARE published schema properties, so their presence is documented rather than unverified; the abbreviated `Key` type in the limits guide simply omits them. `is_provisioning_key` and `rate_limit` are both `deprecated: true`. Two documentation conflicts are recorded rather than resolved: `is_free_tier` is described as "whether the user has paid for credits before" in the limits guide but "Whether this is a free tier API key" in the schema, so it must not be read as a plan name; and the schema documents only 401 and 500 responses for this route, with no 403, unlike GET /api/v1/credits. This fixture sets `workspace_id` to null because management keys are account-scoped and unscoped across workspaces; that null is schema-legal, but it is NOT a measured management-key behaviour and live reconciliation must confirm what a real management key returns here.
